narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have an 11% chance of failing your final year. Because this probability is above the school’s threshold of 10%, you are required to take remedial courses to help ensure your success.

The model considered many aspects of your background and habits, but three factors stood out as most influential in shaping this prediction. The strongest positive influence was your record of not having failed any classes before—this is actually a good sign and helped lower your risk compared to others. Similarly, your clear intention to pursue higher education also worked in your favor, as students with this goal tend to be more motivated and successful; in fact, every student in your group shares this ambition.

However, the main reason your predicted risk is above the threshold is your limited weekly study time. You currently spend less than two hours per week studying, while most students who are not required to take remedial courses dedicate at least two hours or more. This lower study time increased your risk in the model’s eyes, outweighing the positive effects of your clean academic record and future ambitions.

To improve your chances of passing and to potentially move out of the remedial group in the future, consider increasing your study time each week. Taking advantage of the support offered through remedial courses can also help you build stronger study habits and boost your confidence as you approach your final exams.
